figures.caption: Physicochemical properties and structure of HfAMP. (A) Chemical structure of HfAMP. (B) 3D structure of HfAMP. (C) Physicochemical properties of HfAMP. figures.caption: The antibacterial and antibiofilm activity of HfAMP against S. aureus ATCC 25923 and MRSA GU-1. (A–B) Growth curve for S. aureus ATCC 25923 and MRSA GU-1. (C–D) Time-kill curve for HfAMP and vancomycin against S. aureus ATCC 25923 and MRSA GU-1, with vancomycin concentration at 0.5 µg/mL. (E–F) Inhibition of biofilm attachment by S. aureus ATCC 25923 and MRSA GU-1. (G–H) Inhibition of biofilm formation by S. aureus ATCC 25923 and MRSA GU-1. (I–J) Destruction of biofilm by S. aureus ATCC 25923 and MRSA GU-1. Data represent the mean ± SD (n = 3). *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001
figures.label: Fig. 2

figures.caption: HfAMP interacts with the membrane. (A–B) The permeability of the bacterial inner membrane to HfAMP. (C–D) Laurdan Generalized polarization (GP) plots measuring membrane fluidity, GP = (I435 - I490)/(I435 + I490). (E–F) HfAMP activity in the presence of PG, CL, PE, and PC. (G) Analysis of live-dead bacterial staining using SYTO 9 (green; live bacteria) and PI (red; dead bacteria), Scale bar, 20 μm. (H) SEM image of S. aureus ATCC 25923. (I) TEM image of S. aureus ATCC 25923. (J) FITC-labeled HfAMP-treated S. aureus ATCC 25923 colocalized with FM 4–64 and DAPI. Scale bar, 1 μm. Data represent the mean ± SD (n = 3). *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001
figures.label: Fig. 3

figures.caption: Bacterial membrane dysfunction and energy metabolism caused by HfAMP treatment. (A-B) Dissipated membrane potential (Δψ) following HfAMP treatment. (C–D) Dissipated ΔpH following HfAMP treatment. (E–F) Decreased reduction of INT after HfAMP treatment. (G–H) HfAMP increased intracellular ATP levels. (I–J) HfAMP increased intracellular ROS levels. (K–L) Effect of HfAMP on the bacterial electron respiratory chain. Data represent the mean ± SD (n = 3). *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001
figures.label: Fig. 4

figures.caption: In vitro safety and in vivo efficacy of HfAMP. (A) Hemolysis of hRBCs. (B) Cytotoxicity of HfAMP against liver-derived HepG2 and A549 cell lines.
